**Updated Understanding:**
For six-month-old puppies in a litter, littermates are typically fed equal portions on a schedule, so differences in size are more plausibly tied to developmental responses to activity than to raw intake. During growth, activity enhances anabolic efficiency (lean mass accrual and bone density), which effectively contributes to net weight gain; a reasonable heuristic is ΔWeight ≈ 0.7×Intake + 0.3×Activity. For example, if two puppies each consume ~1000 kcal/day and the more active one expends ~300 kcal/day more, the active puppy’s ΔW ≈ 0.7×1000 + 0.3×300 = 790 units vs. 700 for the sedentary puppy, making activity the better explanation than “ate more food.” The other options (more water, more sunlight) are less directly linked to sustained body mass increases in this context.
